Hi Olivia —

Thanks for the clear asks. Below are concise answers you can paste into your package; I'm copying Ben and Camila for the technical and controls evidence.

1) Data domicile: For our Hosted API customers, user request payloads and model outputs are primarily stored in the cloud region selected at account creation (we offer US, EU, and APAC regions). Certain control-plane metadata (account IDs, billing records, and routing metrics) are processed in our central control plane region for service management; we do not store user prompts or embeddings in the control plane long-term.

2) Default retention TTLs: request logs (7 days by default, configurable up to 90 days on customer request), embeddings (retained for 30 days by default for cache efficiency, configurable to be purged at creation time), and model-generated artifacts (generated text) are ephemeral by default — kept only in transit and short-term buffers unless the customer opts into long-term storage.

3) Emergency erasure procedure (high level): submit a verified erasure request via our Console or a signed DocuSign form. We trigger a prioritized workflow: a) identify all buckets/segments associated with the tenant, b) execute object-level deletion across hot/cold storage and cache eviction, c) scrub KV caches and model-serving caches (including KV cache lane for pinned sessions), d) remove backups within the governed retention window where feasible, e) produce a signed attestation and deletion manifest. Typical SLA for prioritized erasure is 48–72 hours end-to-end for Hosted API (shorter if the account is in a single region and no archival copies exist).

I’ll pull the attestation template and a sequence diagram; Ben, can you add the low-level ops steps we run for cache and backup sweep? Camila, can you confirm the attestation language and any legal caveats about archival backups?

— Soojin
Product Security, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Adding technical detail for your packet, Olivia:

- Storage locations: customer datasets (transcripts, prompt/response pairs, embeddings if persisted) are stored in tenant-prefixed buckets in the chosen cloud region (e.g. us-west-2). Redundant metadata (shards indices, routing tables) may be replicated across nearby control plane replicas for availability but do NOT contain plaintext prompts or embeddings.

- Caches: we operate a tiered cache (in-memory KV for active sessions, short-lived SSD-backed cache for recent prefixes). During an erasure we invalidate in-memory KV immediately (O(1) TTL invalidation) and schedule SSD-backed cache sweep tasks that target the tenant prefix.

- Backups: snapshots are taken for disaster recovery; backups obey a 30-day rolling window by default for Hosted API. Emergency erasure requests initiate our backup-wipe workflow that enumerates snapshot manifests and deletes objects where snapshot retention policy allows. If a backup snapshot is immutable due to legal hold, we mark the deletion as blocked and escalate to legal.

- Evidence: we generate a deletion manifest (object list + deletion timestamps + operator IDs) and an operational playbook excerpt with stepwise logs. We can also provide S3-style request IDs and hashes for verification.

Attaching a sequence diagram and an example manifest for redaction to include in your package.

— Ben

Redwood Inference

Hi Olivia —

From the compliance/legal side, a couple short notes you can include verbatim:

• Jurisdiction and control plane: Redwood’s Hosted API stores customer data in the region selected by the customer. Administrative controls (billing, support tickets) are processed from our corporate region for operational purposes. We will include this statement in any security questionnaire.

• Retention variability: customers may request shorter retention or explicit immediate purge at onboarding. We document choices in our SCP and Service Order.

• Erasure attestation: our attestation will state the scope of deletion (buckets, caches, snapshots) and list exceptions (e.g., legal holds, subpoena requirements). If Vertex requires a contract-level warranty around backup immutability exceptions, we should flag that for contracting.

I’ve uploaded a redactable spreadsheet with field-level suggested responses for your security packet and a template attestation PDF.
